0.long_answer: The kidney-shaped structure in question is the spleen. The spleen is an important organ in the immune system and is often evaluated in the staging of pancreatic cancer, as it is a common site where metastatic spread can be detected. Its close anatomical relationship with the tail of the pancreas makes it a critical structure during imaging studies such as CT scans. Detecting metastasis in the spleen helps in determining the stage of the disease, which in turn guides treatment decisions and provides insights into the patient’s overall prognosis.
